findings.element: 'Aufschlüsseln' breakdown selects on report V8 Fahrtausfälle (#fa-auf-1/-2/-3) and report V11 Pünktlichkeit (#punct-auf-1/-2/-3)
findings.finding: The breakdown selects give visible feedback when changed — the cascade greys out the dimension already used in another level — but the table never re-aggregates, so the control looks like it worked while the numbers are still grouped the old way.
findings.user_impact: An analyst who breaks a report down by Kanton or Haltestelle reads TU-level numbers believing they are Kanton-level numbers, which is a wrong-answer failure rather than a visible dead end.
findings.suggested_fix: Make faCascade()/punctCascade() re-render the table from the selected dimensions and update the first column header to the chosen dimension; until the data path exists, disable the selects and label them as not yet available rather than letting them respond.

evidence.action: Headless Chromium: opened 'Fahrtausfälle DPM – Letzte 30 Tage, alle Linien' via its Anzeigen button, then set #fa-auf-1 TU → Kanton and #fa-auf-2 Betriebstag → Linie; separately opened 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH' and changed #punct-auf-1 Linienbündel → Haltestelle → TU konzessioniert.
evidence.observed: V8: row count stayed 22, the tbody text was byte-identical before and after, the header row was unchanged, and the first data rows still read the TU codes AAGL/AAGR — no Kanton anywhere. V11: table stayed at 20 rows with the first column header still 'Name / Line bundle'. In both reports the only visible reaction was options turning grey in the sibling selects. Code confirms it: renderPunctReport() always iterates PUNCT_DATA.bundles and never reads the select values, and faCascade() only sets opt.disabled.

findings.element: Bundle row expander caret (.punct-expand-btn) in the V11 Pünktlichkeit table
findings.finding: The first click on a bundle's expander does nothing at all — line rows only appear on the second click — because the button renders without the .collapsed class while the line rows render already hidden, so the first click re-hides hidden rows.
findings.user_impact: Drilling from a bundle to its lines — the drill-down step of reading a report — reads as broken on first contact, so analysts either give up on the caret or double-click it and land back on a collapsed row.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the expander with the .collapsed class (or derive the toggle from the rows' actual .punct-hidden state instead of the button's class) so the first click expands, and swap the icon glyph between expand_more and expand_less.

evidence.action: Headless Chromium, fresh load: opened 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH' and clicked the first bundle's caret (AAGL BusÜ 1) three times, counting rows without .punct-hidden after each click.
evidence.observed: 20 visible rows initially → 20 after the 1st click (no change whatsoever) → 26 after the 2nd click (6 line rows appear) → 20 again after the 3rd. Confirmed in togglePunctBundle(): it reads btn.classList.contains('collapsed'), which is false on a freshly rendered button, so the first click takes the hide branch.

findings.element: Reports list — 'Done' rows without an 'Anzeigen' action (Rohdaten Export, Linienanalyse DPM, Datenqualitätsindex DPM, and two of the four Done Fahrtausfälle rows)
findings.finding: Nine of the nineteen evaluations marked Done offer no way to open their result and no message explaining why, and two of them are the same report type and status as neighbouring rows that do offer 'Anzeigen'.
findings.user_impact: The very first step of reading a report dead-ends on half the finished evaluations: the status says the work succeeded, the row offers only 'delete', and the user has no idea whether the result is missing, still building, or hidden somewhere else.
findings.suggested_fix: Either give every Done row a working open action, or show the reason in the row (a disabled action with a tooltip such as 'Result available as download only' / 'No report view for this type') so Done never means 'nothing you can do'.

evidence.action: Headless Chromium: logged in and read every reports-list row from the DOM, pairing each row's status chip with the buttons it exposes.
evidence.observed: 19 rows show Done. 10 expose ['Anzeigen','delete']; 9 expose only ['delete'] — 'Rohdaten Export – Gestern', '– Letzte Woche', '– April 2026 komplett', 'Linienanalyse DPM – Letztes Jahr, Kanton BE', '– Letzter Monat, S 1, S 5', '– Aktueller Monat, RE 7, BLS', 'Datenqualitätsindex DPM – Letzter Monat, alle TU', '– Letztes Jahr, SBB, BLS, ZVV', plus 'Fahrtausfälle DPM – Letzter Monat, BLS, Kanton BE' and '– Letztes Jahr, Bahn Normalspur', which sit two rows below Fahrtausfälle entries that do have Anzeigen. No tooltip, empty state or explanatory text accompanies the missing action.

findings.element: Report V11 Pünktlichkeit — header area above the table (no KPI card grid) and the Value column of the Total row
findings.finding: The punctuality report — the one whose whole purpose is a percentage against a threshold — has no KPI cards at all, so the headline 90,84% sits in a table row styled like the twenty rows under it, with no threshold stated and no pass/fail colouring anywhere in the column.
findings.user_impact: An analyst opening the report cannot see at a glance whether punctuality met the target; they have to know that 90% is the threshold and compare it by eye, and a failing 85,18% row looks exactly like a passing 96,62% one.
findings.suggested_fix: Give V11 the same KPI card grid V5 and V8 already have — overall value, threshold, and a ✓/⚠ mark — and apply the same above/below-threshold colouring to the Value column.

evidence.action: Headless Chromium: opened 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH', queried for any KPI card element inside #view-report-punct, and screenshotted the top of the report.
evidence.observed: Zero KPI elements (V5 renders 4 cards each labelled 'Threshold: 90%' with ✓/⚠, V8 renders 3). The markup confirms it: #rpt-kpi-grid exists in view-report-connection and #fa-kpi-grid in view-report-fa, but view-report-punct has no grid. In the screenshot the report goes breadcrumb → title → chips → breakdown strip → table; the Total row's 90,84% is the same size and the same blue as 85,18% and 96,62% below it, and the word 'threshold' appears nowhere on the page.

findings.element: 'Break down by' select options on V11 (#punct-auf-1/-2/-3) in EN mode, and the chip dropdown header 'Transport companies' in DE mode
findings.finding: A single dropdown mixes the two languages: in EN mode the list reads 'No selection, Operating day, Linienbündel, Line, Haltestelle, Monat, CW, TU konzessioniert, TU fahrend, Transport mode, Region', and in DE mode the TU chip panel is headed with the English 'Transport companies'.
findings.user_impact: A non-German-speaking analyst cannot tell what five of the eleven breakdown dimensions are, so they cannot choose the grouping they need — and the mixed list makes the language switch look half-broken rather than half-translated.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the five untranslated options (linienbuendel, haltestelle, monat, tu_konz, tu_fahr) data-i18n keys with EN and DE entries, and give the chip dropdown headers a key so 'Transport companies' becomes 'Transportunternehmen' in DE.

evidence.action: Headless Chromium in the default EN mode: opened 'Pünktlichkeit – Letzter Monat, Kanton ZH' and read the option labels of the three breakdown selects; cross-checked the markup and the DE run recorded in the state map.
evidence.observed: The EN-mode strip reads 'Break down by | Linienbündel | Line | No selection' with the German labels Linienbündel, Haltestelle, Monat, TU konzessioniert and TU fahrend in the open list; the markup shows those five options carry no data-i18n attribute at all (a different mechanism from AUTO-9, where the key exists but the dictionary entry is missing). In DE the chip panel header is the literal string 'Transport companies', also with no data-i18n attribute.
